extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, respondents in USPTO disciplinary proceedings, and USPTO OED/legal staff
extracted.subtask_description: Administrative final order applying 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 to impose reciprocal discipline on a USPTO-registered practitioner, explaining the regulatory standards for imposing identical discipline, available defenses/relief, reinstatement conditions, and publication/notice requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline requirement (37 C.F.R. § 11.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions of 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 require the imposition of 'identical' reciprocal discipline where a practitioner has been disciplined by a state authority, unless the respondent makes a sufficient showing under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office gave Respondent 40 days to file a response opposing identical reciprocal discipline. There is no legal basis to grant a reduced penalty absent a showing under § 11.24(d)(1). The Director concluded Respondent conceded he could not make that showing, so identical discipline was required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible defenses to identical discipline (37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A respondent may oppose imposition of identical reciprocal discipline based on one or more of the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order references § 11.24(d)(1) as the exclusive avenue to avoid identical discipline; Respondent did not dispute imposition of reciprocal discipline on any of those listed factors and thus failed to carry the burden to avoid identical discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nunc pro tunc relief criteria (37 C.F.R. § 11.24(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Discipline may be imposed nunc pro tunc under § 11.24(f) only upon a showing that includes prompt notification of the state discipline to the USPTO, voluntary ceasing practice before the Office, and compliance with all provisions of 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent did not make the requisite showing for nunc pro tunc relief; he conceded delay in communicating state discipline and provided no evidence of compliance with the other § 11.24(f) provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement procedure and eligibility period (37 C.F.R. § 11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall remain suspended from practice before the USPTO until the OED Director grants a petition requesting reinstatement pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60; Respondent is eligible to file a petition requesting reinstatement eighteen (18) months after the effective date of the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order specifies commencement of suspension on the date of the Final Order and that eligibility to petition for reinstatement begins 18 months after that effective date; reinstatement occurs only upon OED Director's grant of a § 11.60 petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condition for reinstatement: MPRE score requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: As a condition of reinstatement, Respondent shall provide satisfactory evidence to the OED Director that he took the Multistate Professional Responsibility Examination (MPRE) after July 15, 2021, and attained a scaled score of 85 or higher thereon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This condition derives from the state-court order and is made a condition for USPTO reinstatement; satisfactory evidence of the specified MPRE score must be presented with the reinstatement petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance with § 11.58 is required as part of reinstatement conditions and is also referenced as one of the prerequisites for nunc pro tunc relief under § 11.24(f). The Order does not restate § 11.58 duties but mandates adherence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice requirements (FOIA Reading Room, Official Gazette, § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order at OED's FOIA Reading Room and publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the Order; the Director shall give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 to disciplinary enforcement agencies in states of admission, to courts of admission, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order includes a model 'Notice of Suspension' for Official Gazette publication and specifies the FOIA Reading Room URL for public access; § 11.59 notice to agencies and courts is mandated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct warranting reciprocal discipline (state-court findings relied upon)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Minnesota Supreme Court found violations of professional conduct rules including: (1) failing to deposit a client's $1,450 filing fees into a trust account, misappropriating those filing fees, neglecting the matter, and failing to communicate with the client; (2) in another matter, failing to communicate, failing to deposit unearned fees into a trust account, and failing to promptly return unearned fees; and (3) failing to maintain proper trust account books and records, resulting in shortages, commingling personal funds with client funds, and allowing a third-party to withdraw funds from the trust account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order ties these factual findings to violations of specific Minnesota Rules of Professional Conduct (e.g., 1.3, 1.4, 1.15, 1.16, 8.4) and uses them as the predicate for imposing reciprocal discipline under USPTO regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard of administrative decision (no genuine issue of material fact)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director determined there was no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and that suspension from practice before the USPTO is the appropriate discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This articulates the administrative standard applied: absent a genuine issue of material fact showing entitlement to relief under the cited provisions, identical reciprocal discipline will be imposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on reduced penalty absent regulatory showing
rubrics_metrics.description: A respondent's request for a 'reduced penalty' is not a lawful basis to avoid identical reciprocal discipline; only a showing under § 11.24(d)(1) or § 11.24(f) can justify departure from identical discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent's plea that identical discipline would be a 'further extension of [his] punishment' was insufficient without citation to or reliance upon applicable authority; the Office denied the request for a reduced penalty on that basis.
